payment-graph.name: email domain + country + ip/16 + name shape
payment-graph.description: Accounts that share an email provider, a country, a /16 network and a user name of the same shape (letters before the digits). The regular expression contributes its formula, not what it matched, so zhang1988 and xia1999 are linked.

payment-graph.name: ip/24 + machine-made email + card BIN
payment-graph.description: Accounts whose email local part is four digits, on the same /24 network and with the same card BIN. The regular expression contributes its shape to the key, so any address of that shape counts.
payment-graph.demoTitle: pattern -> the accounts that share the key

payment-graph.name: Login -> BalanceCheck -> Payment -> Dispute, each within 100s
payment-graph.description: One account's event list, read in time order: a Login, a BalanceCheck, a Payment and a Dispute, all four present, the steps at most 100 seconds apart. The key is the /24 of the login address and the dispute reason, so accounts whose sessions look alike (same network, same reason) land on one link node. Extra events in the list are ignored; a missing step, a longer gap or a value the step needs that is not there makes the pattern not apply.
payment-graph.demoTitle: pattern -> the accounts whose session looks the same

payment-graph.name: Login then a disputed payment on the same /24, within 5 minutes
payment-graph.description: The same idea with a wider window, a /24 in the key and the reason as a condition rather than as part of the key: it fires on a login followed by a payment and a dispute within five minutes each, and only when the reason is NotMyCard. Accounts that share the network are linked.
payment-graph.demoTitle: pattern -> the accounts on the same network
